text.p: Italy's debt market put on a late spurt to end at session highs on the back of softer U.S. data after a day marked by flat to weaker prices, traders said.
The turnaround came in the last hour of trading, due to a general rally on bond markets after the June NAPM index came in at 55.7 against an expected 56.4 and May's 57.1
"The market is now less apprehensive about a rate hike from the Fed's FOMC (meeting today and Wednesday)," said one trader.
Operators said the underlying tone of the market remained positive even if "at these levels there's no queue of buyers, there's more a desire to take profits."
Traders noted that the September Liffe Btp contract held up well today around the 133.75/80 support level.
"There's not a lot of space on the upside," one said. "After last week's drive the market want's to pause for breath," he said noting that traded volumes were well off recent levels.
In cash bonds, the February 1, 2007 bond ended 36 basis points up at 100.32, yielding 6.80 percent, with the spread over the benchmark Bund at 114 bps after narrowing in to 113.
